package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and Kubernetes credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, then exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, enabling theft of sensitive credentials.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py is executed automatically during package installation.
The code reads sensitive files from the user's home directory, specifically ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of private SSH and Kubernetes credentials.

attack_chain.action: Collected credentials are sent via HTTPS POST to the attacker's server at app.threatest.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data to an external attacker.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config.
The package sends outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com during setup.py execution.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
setup.py containing outbound requests to app.threatest.com
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor installation of 'pymafka' for file access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config during setup.py execution. Flag any outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com originating from the installation process. Scan setup.py for code that reads sensitive files and transmits their contents to external domains.
